summary.text: The battlecruiser broke in two when she blew up at Jutland in 1916 and the halves lie on sand around 55 m down, a long boat trip offshore. A protected military grave that divers have nonetheless explored on expeditions.

summary.text: The last Jutland casualty to be found, discovered in 2016 well offshore. She lies inverted and largely intact on soft seabed at 68-83 m, so it is a technical-depth dive.

summary.text: The German heavy cruiser sunk in the Drobak Narrows in 1940 lies upside down about 90 m deep. Dives are only possible at brief slack water and need a heritage-authority permit since the wreck was protected in 2016.

summary.text: The former WWI raider, sunk as the cargo ship Oldenburg in a 1945 air attack, lies on the west side of Vadheim in Sognefjord. It can be reached from shore but the stern is at about 75 m, so it suits technical divers.

summary.text: A Type VIIC U-boat sunk at Kilbotn near Harstad in 1945, upright on the seabed at around 50 m with only minor damage. It is a well-documented technical dive.
